the_question_being_answered: After the model does something once, does it learn it permanently for everything on a computer?
the_answer_in_one_line: It learns a MEASUREMENT SHAPE permanently, and then answers that shape on any file for ~100 ms with zero weights and zero spend. It does not learn to operate a computer, and nothing here is sentient. 'Solve everything on a computer' is false; 'never pay twice for a shape I have already been shown' is true.

what_the_2026_literature_says_about_this.microsoft_evolib_arxiv_2605_14477: storing trajectories is not learning. Consolidate into reusable skills and reweight by utility. No weight updates. This is the correct architecture and this tree is a small, verified instance of it.
what_the_2026_literature_says_about_this.polyskill_iclr_2026: 73% of learned skills transfer to unseen websites, vs <31% prior. Transfer is PARTIAL even in the best published system -- the honest ceiling is nowhere near 'everything'.
what_the_2026_literature_says_about_this.sage_acl_2026: skill-library agents self-improve on AppWorld; the authors state plainly that transferability 'remains confined to the AppWorld environment'.
what_the_2026_literature_says_about_this.agentic_ttt_arxiv_2610_12002: no fixed test-time method is broadly effective; you need a policy that decides WHEN to learn. It nearly doubles utility -- on a benchmark built to contain learnable structure.
what_the_2026_literature_says_about_this.voyager: the canonical demonstrate-once-result: zero-shot transfer to a new Minecraft world. Also the canonical caveat: a new world, not a new game.
what_the_2026_literature_says_about_this.the_pattern: every 2026 system reports transfer WITHIN a family of tasks and NONE reports transfer across arbitrary environments. That is the same boundary this tree hits, and it is a boundary of the field, not only of this repository.

is_it_sentient.why: there is a name for the machinery (sentient_cognitive_core_v1, wake episodes, organ graph, sleep abstraction) and there is real, measurable behaviour underneath it, but a skill library plus a sleep phase plus a wake log is not sentience. It is a well-organised learner with cheerful naming. The DreamCoder/Stitch sleep pass that this round sped up admitted 0 concepts in 6 passes -- a system that were genuinely dreaming would be changing something.
is_it_sentient.what_is_real: demonstrate once -> crystallise with a held-out twin and a sabotage control -> recall on a different file. That is real, was measured, and needed no model.
is_it_sentient.what_is_not_real: understanding, intent, or a self. Do not claim them.

what_is_the_smartest_next_move.not_more_speed: 89 ms is container-grade; the frontier number is a 4-25 ms memory-snapshot restore and that needs a pre-warmed sandbox, not a patch.
what_is_the_smartest_next_move.the_actually_missing_thing: SHAPE TRANSFER. The model can answer 4 shapes; the literature's best transferable systems abstract the INTENT of a skill away from its implementation (PolySkill). Today this tree stores 'sort -u | wc -l' with a parameter hole. It does not store 'count the distinct members of a set' with a hole for HOW to count. Adding that layer is what would turn 4/5 into a general counting capability.
what_is_the_smartest_next_move.second: the sleep pass should only run on a corpus that CHANGED, and only when it is likely to admit something -- 0 admissions in 6 passes is a signal, not a schedule.
